Chairman, Sena Kalyan Sangstha ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Sufi Fazal Ahmed and others  -----  Opposite Parties
full_judgment: 2. Facts leading to this Rule are very simple. Plaintiff opposite party Haji Fazal Ahmed, who was originally a man of Gujrat came over to Bangladesh in Chittagong in 1945 and started residing here permanently with family members acquiring citizenship of Bangladesh. The plaintiff took settlement for 99 years of a piece of landed property by a registered deed of lease in 1966, from the Govt. in the Chittagong industrial estate. Thereafter, the plaintiff started his industry with the name and style Metal Industries on the suit land. The industry was a private limited company. The eldest son of the plaintiff Nazar Mainuddin was the Managing Director of the said industry. The plaintiff keeping his son Nazar Mainuddin in the management and control of the said industry left Bangladesh on 25-11-71 to perform Haj Pilgrimage in Mecca. Because of the liberation war taking serious form in the last part of 1971 and because the plaintiff is an Urdu speaking man, he could not return to Bangladesh in 1971 or thereafter. The plaintiff came back to Bangladesh on 10-9-76 on a Pakistani Passport. Thereafter, he made an application for citizenship afresh as needed at that time because of circumstance prevailing in Bangladesh then. The plaintiff of course, after his return here in Bangladesh expressed his allegiance to Bangladesh and its Government on. 7-4-78, the plaintiff was given citizenship afresh by the Bangladesh Government. but in the meantime on 20-12-71, the possession and management of the said industry which is the suit property was taken over by the Government on the basis of President's Order 1 of 1972. Subsequently, the said industry was treated as abandoned property in terms of President's Order 16 of 1972 and it was sold and was delivered to the possession and control of the defendant No. 5 Sena Kalyan Sangstha of Bangladesh Army and it also appears that the deed which is Ext. C by which the said business concern of the plaintiff was sold to the said Sena Kallyan Sangstha is dated 4-10-80 and the transfer was made for Taka 1000.00 only as token price. The plaintiff unsuccessfully moved from door to door to get his property released and to get his possession but in vain and thereafter he filed writ petition being No.618/80, but the same was treated as abated by operation of law and lastly, the petitioner has instituted the present suit for declaration of his title in the suit property and to get khas possession of the same and also for mesne profits.
